title: HyRec2011 analytic helium recombination: fit, conditioning and rate conventions

scopes.title: HeII to HeI analytic line treatment and explicit approximation boundaries
scopes.checked_claim: Section VI assumes one temperature T_m=T_r, HeI excited levels in equilibrium with the continuum, and a small hydrogen neutral fraction treated with Saha equilibrium. The 584 Angstrom line uses steady radiation transfer, damping wings and hydrogen continuum opacity; its width contribution Gamma_other includes the 2P-to-2S transition and selected n=3-5 singlet levels. Eq.117 fits its dimensionless enhancement as sqrt(1+pi^2*tau_c)+7.74*tau_c/(1+70*tau_c), stated within 0.8% for all positive tau_c, with limit 1 at zero. The 591 Angstrom intercombination line uses the full Sobolev absorption factor and on-the-spot feedback that subtracts P_reabs*F584. These fit statements differ from the reported maximum 0.3% helium-history comparison in VI.4. The later pinned helium.c variant uses cm, seconds and Kelvin and returns d(x_HeII)/dln(a), with species fractions per H nucleus and x_e=1-x_HI+x_HeII; it is a distinct source convention, not a total-electron rate or an erratum to the paper.
scopes.unresolved: The HTML literally prints dot(x_e)=-F in Eq.99 and F(H)=-dot(x_HI)|Saha in Eq.121 while summing all F contributions. Their combination has a sign tension with the stated charge identity; original PDF/journal comparison and source convention reconciliation remain open. Exact energy-zero/temperature-unit mapping, adopted atomic inputs, caller species normalization, approximation errors, integration/domain controls, native adapter and solved thermal history are separate requirements. No full HeIII kinetics, independently evolved coupled H/He law, likelihood or physical CMB qualification follows.

source_assets.conditioning: Selected Section VI, definitions and conclusions only. Eqs.117,99,121 original MathML/alttext checked; figure images and original PDF not inspected. The reported history comparison uses the source flat LCDM conditioning, not a new numerical guarantee.

limitations: The source fit error is an author-stated approximation error, with no statistical distribution, sigma interpretation or covariance supplied. It is not a bound on the whole recombination history.
The historical 0.3% comparison and conclusions' few-times-10^-3 helium estimate retain source cosmology, approximations and collision caveats; no new physical or numerical qualification.
Eq.99/Eq.121 HTML signs remain literal and unresolved. The charge-chain derivation and later HeII source interface do not silently repair the paper or establish an author erratum.

The 2011 paper's equilibrium/switching assumptions differ from the source code's 2012 explicit hydrogen input and 2015 density-unit change. Same fit coefficients do not establish complete variant equivalence.

A per-He caller must bind its conversion to per-H source fractions and keep the hydrogen contribution separate. Temperature/atomic-energy conventions and source approximation domains must be matched before an adapter is accepted.

Original PDF/figures, antecedent references, complete error budgets and legal/vendoring terms remain unexamined; raw sources are not redistributed. Full HeIII kinetics, coupled thermodynamics and CMB/likelihood scope remain open.
